chunks: The shares of inheritance came to be six portions and do not exceed that because the human being was created from six things,
and this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
And indeed, We created man from an extract of clay.
And another reason is that the people of inheritance who inherit permanently and are never excluded are six: the two parents, the son, the daughter, the husband, and the wife.

key_terms.سُلَالَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ: an extract of clay, referring to the origin of human creation
key_terms.سِتَّةِ أَسْهُمٍ: six legal portions into which inheritance shares are arranged
key_terms.لَا يُسْقَطُونَ: they are not excluded from inheritance

ai.seo_question: Why are the shares of inheritance set at six portions in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام explains that the inheritance shares are arranged upon six portions. It connects this legal structure to the creation of the human being and also states that the permanently entitled inheritors who are never excluded are six: the parents, son, daughter, husband, and wife.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5604 - Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"The shares of inheritance were set at six portions and do not exceed that because the human being was created from six elements,
as stated in the words of Allah (swt), the Majestic:
'And indeed, We created man from an extract of clay.' (Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:12).
Another reason is that the inheritors who always inherit and are never excluded are six: the two parents, the son, the daughter, the husband, and the wife."
